sentences.text: Mesadactylus is an extinct pterosaur genus found in the Upper Jurassic Morrison Formation of Colorado, United States.

The type species of the genus is Mesadactylus ornithosphyos, based on the holotype specimen, BYU 2024, which consists of a synsacrum made of seven fused sacral vertebrae with a unique complete fusion of spinae into a supraneural blade.
Associated remains include arm bones, pectoral girdle bones, vertebrae, and femora.
The genus Mesadactylus was named in 1989 by James Jensen and Kevin Padian.
Additional material, including a partial braincase, was described in 2004 and 2006.
Mesadactylus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, between 152.21 and 145.06 million years ago.
Jensen and Padian originally classified Mesadactylus as a pterodactyloid.

In 2007, S. Christopher Bennett claimed that the holotype and referred material came from different forms, arguing the synsacrum belonged to an Anurognathidae member while the rest was pterodactyloid, a view that questions whether Mesadactylus belongs to the family Anurognathidae.
